gadgets.versions: 13.0.3 (measured live; applies to every version, this is configuration rather than a CVE)
gadgets.sink: JsonConvert.DeserializeObject called with JsonSerializerSettings { TypeNameHandling = All | Objects | Auto | Arrays } on attacker-influenced JSON
gadgets.effect: the JSON names the CLR type to construct, and Json.NET then sets each named property. Look in the APPLICATION'S OWN assembly before reaching for a published gadget chain: a class whose property setter has a side effect is a complete one-object gadget. Nexus Void shipped Nexus_Void.Helpers.StatusCheckHelper, whose `command` setter builds a ProcessStartInfo for /bin/bash -c and runs it, so {"$type":"Nexus_Void.Helpers.StatusCheckHelper, Nexus_Void","command":"<cmd>"} is RCE with no ysoserial and no chain.
gadgets.precondition: TypeNameHandling is anything other than None, and no SerializationBinder restricts the types. The assembly name in $type must be the ASSEMBLY, not the namespace; for a project named Nexus_Void both happen to read the same and that hides the distinction.
gadgets.trap: the cast AFTER deserialisation is irrelevant. The application here does `deserialized as List<ProductModel>`, which yields null for the gadget, and the page then renders as if nothing happened -- but the setter already ran while the object was being built. Do not read an unchanged page as the payload having failed. Corollary: the command's output is not returned, so plan how it comes back before sending it (a copy into a served wwwroot needs no listener).
